newsitem.title: USA: Stocks little changed after morning gyrations.
newsitem.headline: Stocks little changed after morning gyrations.

text.p: Stocks hovered nearly unchanged Friday after key economic reports provided fresh evidence of a slow-growing economy with scant inflationary pressures.
Just after 1:15 p.m., the Dow Jones industrial average was off 10.81 points at 6,018.57.

The 30-share index was weighed down by Boeing, which fell 3 to 92-3/8 after the company said development of its next generation of 747 jumbo-jets could cost up to $7 billion, more than had been expected.
In the broader market, losing issues narrowly outnumbered gainers on heavy volume of 277 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq composite index rose 0.71 point to 1,222.22.
The government said the unemployment rate was unchanged at 5.2 percent in October, with job growth at a moderate 210,000, in line with expectations.
Other reports also pointed to slowing economic growth with little inflationary pressures.
"The economic data are pointing to a relatively slow economy and not a particularly big inflation problem," said Roy Blumberg, chief investment strategist at Josephthal Lyon & Ross.
The government also said September factory orders rose 2.7 percent, fuelled mostly by new aircraft orders that more than offset weakness in other product categories.

Two reports by private groups added to a picture of moderating activity. A survey of the nation's purchasing managers showed that the manufacturing sector grew more slowly in October than in September. And a key forecasting gauge rose for the eighth straight month, though it was the smallest gain in that string of increases.
The reports come just two days after the government said the economy slowed to a 2.2 percent rate of growth in the third quarter from a brisk 4.7 percent rate in the second quarter.
Bonds lost ground after rallying on economic news earlier in the week. The bellwether 30-year Treasury bond fell 11/32, or $3.44 on a $1,000 bond, raising its yield to 6.67 percent from 6.64 percent.

Analysts said there was some renewed focus on Tuesday's elections, though there was less fear of a Democratic sweep of both houses of Congress. President Clinton's re-election was deemed a near certainty.
"The House election is important. But there are lessened concerns about the House and a sweep of Congress," said Peter Canelo, chief investment strategist at Dean Witter.
Among individual issues, Inference Corp. lost 5-1/4 to 7 after the software maker warned that third-quarter results would be well below expectations.
Samsonite surged 3-1/4 to 37 after it said late on Thursday it would restructure and cut 450 jobs.
The American Stock Exchange index added 2.71 points to 571.43.
